headers.title: Headers and constants
headers.text: The site as Referer on covers; COVER_ATTR the image attribute that held a real address; FRAME the element that holds the player on an episode page, where the video finder starts.

getPopular.title: Popular
getPopular.text: The home page's title links (/anime/… and poster cards), one page. A site with a /popular page can point this at it.

getLatest.title: Latest
getLatest.text: The home page's episode links folded back to their title, one page.

search.title: Search
search.text: /search?keyword=words; some sites use /search?q= or /?s= instead, which is a one-line change.

getDetails.title: Title page
getDetails.text: The h1 or og:title, og:image as cover, the description block or og:description, genre links.

getChapterList.title: Episodes
getChapterList.text: Every episode link of the title page, each address once, numbered from data-number, the text or the address, returned oldest first.

getVideoList.title: Videos
getVideoList.text: The app's video finder (host.findVideo) opens the episode page in the hidden browser, presses Play and catches the .m3u8 / .mpd / .mp4 the player asks for, also when the site's script fills in the player's address after the page loads; when nothing comes, the FRAME player itself is opened with the page as Referer. Each video keeps the Referer it was asked with and its player's server group; a master playlist is split into one entry per quality. Nothing caught: the error says why in plain words (no player, the player never asked, pieces without a playlist, the page didn't load). The quality and server settings, when the source has them, put the preferred videos first.

helpers.title: Helpers
helpers.text: One request with the site as Referer, the title-card parser, absolute addresses and the first number of a text.

2.note: Videos use the app's video finder: plays players whose address the site's script fills in and catches DASH.
